easy.q: Sister Muñoz Spannaus told about driving to the dentist. What went wrong on the way?
options: Her phone ran out of power on the freeway
Her GPS kept telling her to turn where she could not
Her car stopped and she had to walk
easy.why: The GPS thought she was on a parallel street, so it kept telling her to turn right “when there was no place to turn.” She pulled off and called her husband for help.

easy.q: After the GPS story, what did Sister Muñoz Spannaus say the Lord knows about you?
options: Only what you tell Him in your prayers
Mostly the mistakes you have made
Exactly where you are and how to guide you
easy.why: She taught, “the Lord knows where you are; He has your exact location and can guide you.” He also knows your dreams, your gifts and your questions.

easy.q: A young man ran to Jesus and asked how to gain eternal life. What did Jesus do before He answered?
options: He looked at him and loved him
He asked him to come back later
He told him he had done enough
easy.why: Sister Muñoz Spannaus read from Mark 10:21: “Jesus beholding him loved him.” The Savior showed His love first.

easy.q: Sister Muñoz Spannaus felt very sad after teaching in English, a language she was still learning. What helped her feel the heavens open?
options: A good night of sleep
A kind note from her class
A priesthood blessing from her husband
easy.why: She went to sleep in tears and woke up feeling the same. Then her husband gave her a priesthood blessing, and she said, “in that moment, I felt the heavens open.”

easy.q: At the end of her talk, what did Sister Muñoz Spannaus invite young women to do?
options: Give up their cell phones for a month
Make their own list of good things to aim for
Learn to speak a second language
easy.why: She said, “I invite you to study the thirteenth article of faith and to create your own list of aspirations,” just as she did when she was a young woman.

medium.q: As a young woman, Sister Muñoz Spannaus spent a Sunday afternoon writing a list. What kind of things did she put on it?
options: Faults she had to fix before she could serve
Good things that would bring her closer to God
Callings she hoped to receive someday
Rules she would keep more strictly than her friends
medium.why: The thirteenth article of faith set her thinking about her aspirations. She listed good, positive things that would bring her closer to God and help her learn, contribute, create and be happy.

medium.q: Sister Muñoz Spannaus said the Lord knows everything about you. What did she say that knowledge does to His love for you?
options: It makes His love grow as each weakness is overcome
It makes Him love most those with the fewest faults
It does not make Him love you any less
It leads Him to overlook what you do wrong
medium.why: After listing what the Lord knows, including your challenges and weaknesses, she said, “knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less.”

medium.q: According to Sister Muñoz Spannaus, what is part of the love and mercy our Father and our Savior have for us?
options: Taking away our challenges once our goals are righteous
Showing us the whole journey before we begin it
Giving each of us the very same work to do
Giving us many chances and being patient as we learn
medium.why: She taught that part of Their love and mercy is “giving us many opportunities and being patient as we learn and work on our list of aspirations.”

medium.q: What did Sister Muñoz Spannaus teach about the work each young woman has to do here on earth?
options: It differs for each person but can bring the same great joy
It is the same for everyone but brings each a different joy
It begins only after she has finished her schooling
It is revealed mainly through the callings she is given
medium.why: She said the work “is different for each person,” but if you choose to love God and Jesus Christ and trust Them, doing it “will bring you the same great joy.”

medium.q: Sister Muñoz Spannaus shared seven ways to help young women in their work. What did she invite them to do with the seven?
options: Begin all seven together this week
Start with whichever one seems hardest
Listen to the Spirit and choose one to focus on
Ask a parent or leader to pick one for them
medium.why: She did not ask for all seven at once: “I invite you to listen to the Spirit to choose one to focus on over the next few weeks.”

hard.q: Which situation best follows the pattern Sister Muñoz Spannaus pointed out in how Jesus treated the young man in Mark 10?
options: A leader holds back warmth until a young woman improves
A leader helps a young woman feel loved, then suggests how to grow
A leader shows love and so never mentions anything to improve
A leader gives correction quickly, then offers comfort afterward
hard.why: She noted the order: the Savior's look conveyed only love, and “Only after transmitting that love did He tell him what he could do to improve.” Love came first, and the counsel still came.

hard.q: Sister Muñoz Spannaus said to begin each day by asking the Father for “that companionship.” Whose companionship did she mean, and where did she say it is promised?
options: Ministering angels’, promised to those who study about them
The Holy Ghost’s, promised in the sacrament as we keep our covenants
The Holy Ghost’s, promised in a priesthood blessing when we are sad
Faithful friends’, promised by the prophet to those who seek them
hard.why: Her morning counsel follows from the sacrament: we partake “grateful for the promise that as you keep your covenants, the Holy Ghost will be your constant companion,” and then each day we ask the Father for that companionship.

hard.q: Which young woman’s scripture study best fits the desire Sister Muñoz Spannaus counseled young women to study with?
options: One reads a set number of pages each night in order to finish by the end of the year
One searches for verses that will help her win a discussion with a classmate
One reads how Jesus treated someone and asks what it shows about what God is like
One studies maps and dates to master the history behind each scripture story
hard.why: Her counsel was to study “with a desire to know God’s character so you can do His will, increase your love for Him, and advance His work.” The aim is to come to know Him, not only to finish or to gather facts.

hard.q: Sister Muñoz Spannaus said to limit cell phone use. What exactly did she say is the trouble with social media?
options: It makes us feel connected while stealing real connection
It fills hours that should all be given to study
It ties us mostly to people who do not share our standards
It harms us in any amount, so phones should be put away
hard.why: She said social media “makes us believe we are connected,” yet it is a thief of our peace of mind, self-esteem and the real connection we feel face to face. Her counsel was to limit use, not to give it up.

hard.q: A young woman gives a lesson, feels it went badly, and wonders why she was ever asked. Which thought best fits what Sister Muñoz Spannaus learned from her own such experience?
options: The feeling will pass once she has practiced enough to avoid mistakes
The feeling is a sign that this assignment was not meant for her
The feeling is one to sleep on, since rest by itself will lift it
The adversary wants to tear down her worth, yet the Godhead is at her side
hard.why: Sleep did not lift her sadness. In a priesthood blessing she was told, “Satan wants to destroy your self-esteem, your mind, your thoughts, and your spirit,” and then, “But the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are at your side.”
